meta.title: Why Epicurus said death is nothing to fear

plates.query: Nicolas Poussin Et in Arcadia Ego painting
Philippe de Champaigne Vanitas skull tulip hourglass
marble bust of Epicurus ancient sculpture

beats.text: Most of our quiet dread, Epicurus said, comes down to one thing: the fear of death.
So he built an argument to dissolve it — not to comfort you, but to reason you free.
"Death is nothing to us," he wrote. And he meant it literally.
While you exist, death is not here. When death comes, you no longer exist to meet it.
The two never touch. So there is no moment in which death can actually harm you.
You did not suffer in the eternity before your birth. The dark after is no different.
Fear steals the life you do have. Spend it, he said, on simple joys and good friends.
